questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language spoken at the host institution, prestige related to the institution, courses offered

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not happy with the educational level at Osaka University. Many of the English based courses were taught by teachers who barely spoke English. Furthermore, most of the academic courses were not on par with the difficulty of courses offered in Denmark. The Japanese language class was amazing and everything I needed it to be, but most of the academic courses were not “academic”.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Osaka university is very good at helping their incoming students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I used the company “Dormy” which both has a department in the Tokyo area and in Kansai

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s just like living off campus in Denmark

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to send an email with an excel document stating what courses I wanted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the exchange office for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to pick classes with foreign professors if you want to learn anything

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level in most of the courses at Osaka university is at most high school level. The courses taught by foreign professors were good, but the courses taught by Japanese professors were not even close to being academic - most likely from an extreme language barrier

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As an example of how lacklustre the level of education is at Osaka University, I had a professor who twice told us fake news because she hadn’t researched it further herself. I had another professor who ended almost every class early because he “isn’t good at English” (it was an English mediated course).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is more aligned with high school or folkeskole in Denmark - there’s not a lot of critical thinking done by the student, but we were instead just fed information

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The price of public transportation is high, as Osaka university does not allow their exchange students to get a student pass for public transportation. This is something other Japanese universities offer, so that was very disappointing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very cheap in Osaka and you can definitely use less than I did if you want to. We didn’t have to buy ANY books

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We were free to join any club at the university if said club allowed exchange students (most do). I joined the cheerleading club. Furthermore, the exchange office and institutions supported by the exchange office offers plenty of cultural events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club! It’s a good way to speak to native students. I also liked “project help” which is a tutor project where the exchange students help a native student with preparing for the IELTS exam

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Osaka is in the middle of the Kansai area so please use that! You can travel to Kyoto, Nara, and Wakayama easily, meaning you can see so much or Japan very easily

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, but I also study Japanese so I had an easier time

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It’s difficult if you don’t speak Japanese as most Japanese students do not speak English

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier. Even if you speak Japanese, Osaka Japanese is very different and difficult to understand

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Personally I just liked experiencing every day life. There wasn’t one specific thing I appreciated the most, it was the entire experience that was worthwhile

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not pick academic classes based on your interests if those classes are on a Friday or Monday. It’s better to have a longer weekend, because the class will most likely disappoint you.
Join a club or project help!
Osaka is known for its food and lively nightlife. Please explore that aspect of the city!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Bettering my Japanese and joining a club. I made many fond memories

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
